page: Microsoft Azure L16s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for data-intensive enterprise workloads requiring dense local capacity and high I/O throughput. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on the x86_64 architecture at 4.2 GHz, the instance delivers 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It includes 128 GB of system RAM—providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio—and features a large 260 MB L3 cache alongside advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Storage capability is anchored by a directly attached 3,840 GB NVMe SSD, avoiding network storage latencies and offering low-latency scratch and transactional operational space. The instance contains no discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarking, the L16s_v4 demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, landing in the top quartile for Geekbench single-core testing (2,162.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (31.49 GB/sec). It also achieved top-tier throughput in small-model text generation inference at 369.86 tokens per second. Multi-threaded evaluations, including stress-ng multi-core and PassMark database operations (9,516.52), consistently fall within the middle 50% band.

From an infrastructure and cost-efficiency standpoint, the integrated 3.84 TB NVMe disk eliminates separate network disk provisioning costs for high-IOPS applications, achieving a practical balance between dense compute, elevated memory, and local persistence. The primary tradeoff lies in the ephemeral nature of direct-attached NVMe storage, which requires application-level replication or dedicated snapshotting strategies for persistent data survival. Azure L16s_v4 is strategically suited for high-throughput relational and NoSQL databases, transactional indexing, Redis caching clusters, real-time analytics, and data-heavy ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L16s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 128 GB of memory, 260 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Local storage consists of a bundled 3,840 GB NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPU is present. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits strong single-threaded performance, placing in the top quartile for Geekbench single-core score and gzip compression, with top-tier throughput on lightweight text generation. General multi-core throughput and database operation benchmarks perform reliably within median thresholds. The high ratio of local NVMe storage to compute resources makes the L16s_v4 cost-effective for I/O-intensive workloads, including transactional databases, Redis deployments, and analytical search engines requiring rapid local caching.
